messages.author: 26f0f6fad1bd9ad7
messages.subject: Translate R functions into Nimble
parts:
Hi,

I'm a new Nimble user and work on the calibration of posterior predictive p-values of bivariate residuals. I have to translate a number of R functions like count() in the ''plyr' package, apply() in the "base", xtabs() in "stats" and combn() etc. Is there any more efficient way to do so?

Thank you in advance.

Best wishes,

Yan

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Translate R functions into Nimble
parts:
Dear Yan,

There are three ways you could consider using or translating such functions.  

1. You could translate them into nimbleFunctions.  Obviously that provides limited features but can work well for primarily numerical functions.

2. You could translate them to C/C++/Fortran and call them from nimbleFunctions as an externalCall (see help(nimbleExternalCall)).

3. You could call them from nimbleFunctions an R calls, which are executed in R, even from compiled nimbleFunctions.  Often a wrapper will be needed to achieve clean types.  Although this can impose some performance cost due to R execution, it is the fastest way to make them work.  See help(nimbleRcall).

Regarding posterior predictive p-values, we are under way implementing the calibrated ppp method of Hjort et al. (JASA 2006, DOI 10.1198/016214505000001393).  Let us know if that is what you are looking for.

Perry

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Translate R functions into Nimble
parts:
You can't use a formula as an object in compiled nimble code.  You would have to wrap your call to xtabs in another R function that you could call from a nimbleFunction and that would then call xtabs and provide the formula.  If the formula is always the same, doing it this way should be easy.  If it is one from a simple set of options, you could pass an integer argument to select the one you need, or use some similar kind of approach.
-Perry
